question: If the speed of a wave is 300 m/s and its wavelength is 0.75 m, the frequency of the wave is __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 400 Hz.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For any wave, speed (v) = frequency (f) × wavelength (λ), so frequency f = v/λ. (तरंग वेग = आवृत्ति × तरंगदैर्ध्य)

 

• Here v = 300 m/s and λ = 0.75 m, so f = 300/0.75 = 400 Hz.

 

• Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), named after Heinrich Hertz, and represents the number of complete oscillations (waves) passing a point per second.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wavelength (λ) is the distance between two consecutive crests or two consecutive troughs of a wave, measured in metres.

 

• Time period (T) is the time taken for one complete oscillation; f = 1/T.

 

• The speed of sound in air is about 344 m/s, while the speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s.

 

NOTE

 

• 225 Hz (Option A): Would result from an incorrect division (e.g. 300 × 0.75), not the correct formula v/λ.

 

• 300 Hz (Option B): Simply the numerical value of speed, ignoring the wavelength altogether.

 

• 75 Hz (Option C): Obtained if wavelength were mistakenly taken as 4 m instead of 0.75 m.

question: The gas released on the reaction of metal carbonate with hydrochloric acid turns lime water milky. The released gas is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a metal carbonate reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl), it produces a metal chloride, water and carbon dioxide gas. (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड — चूने के पानी को दूधिया करती है)

 

• Example: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑.

 

• Carbon dioxide turns lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) milky because it forms insoluble calcium carbonate: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃↓ (milky) + H₂O. On passing excess CO₂, the milkiness disappears as soluble calcium bicarbonate, Ca(HCO₃)₂, is formed.

 

• This reaction is a standard laboratory test to confirm the presence of CO₂ gas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metal bicarbonates also release CO₂ on reacting with acids, similar to carbonates.

 

• CO₂ does not support combustion and is used in fire extinguishers for this reason.

 

• Reaction of a metal with a dilute acid (like zinc with HCl) instead releases hydrogen gas, tested using a burning matchstick that produces a 'pop' sound.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen (Option A): Released when reactive metals react with dilute acids, not carbonates; it burns with a pop sound.

 

• Chlorine (Option C): A greenish-yellow, pungent gas released, for example, during electrolysis of brine, not from this reaction.

 

• Carbon monoxide (Option D): A colourless, odourless, poisonous gas formed by incomplete combustion of carbon fuels, unrelated to this reaction.

question:
A 1000 kg car moving at 10 m/s is brought to rest by a constant braking force in 5 s.

What is the magnitude of the force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2000 N.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's second law of motion, Force (F) = mass (m) × acceleration (a). (बल = द्रव्यमान × त्वरण)

 

• Since the car comes to rest, its deceleration a = (change in velocity)/time = (10 − 0)/5 = 2 m/s².

 

• Force F = m × a = 1000 × 2 = 2000 N. The force acts opposite to the direction of motion, which is why it is called a braking (retarding) force.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's first law (law of inertia): a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

 

• Newton's third law: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

• The SI unit of force is the newton (N), defined as the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a mass of 1 kg.

 

NOTE

 

• 3000 N, 1500 N, 2500 N (Options B, C, D): These result from using an incorrect deceleration value instead of the correctly calculated 2 m/s².

question: Which of the following methods is an example of asexual reproduction in plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vegetative propagation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction in which a new plant grows from a vegetative part of the parent plant — root, stem or leaf — without the fusion of gametes. (कायिक प्रवर्धन — अलैंगिक प्रजनन)

 

• Since only one parent is involved and no gametes fuse, the offspring produced are genetically identical (clones) to the parent plant.

 

• Common natural examples: potato (stem tuber), onion and garlic (bulbs), ginger (rhizome), Bryophyllum (leaf buds). Artificial methods include cutting, grafting and layering, widely used in horticulture (e.g. rose, sugarcane, banana).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fertilisation is the fusion of a male and a female gamete to form a zygote — the defining step of sexual reproduction.

 

• Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma; it precedes fertilisation in sexual reproduction and is not itself reproduction.

 

• Germination is the process by which a seed develops into a seedling; it is a growth stage that follows sexual reproduction, not a mode of reproduction itself.

 

NOTE

 

• Fertilisation (Option A): A step of sexual, not asexual, reproduction.

 

• Germination (Option B): Sprouting of a seed, a stage of plant growth.

 

• Pollination (Option C): Transfer of pollen, a prerequisite for sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

question: Providing water to crops at optimal times during their growth cycle directly contributes to what outcome?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Higher expected yields.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Irrigation at the correct growth stage ensures that crops receive adequate moisture exactly when they need it most (e.g. germination, flowering, grain-filling), which directly improves nutrient absorption and crop productivity, leading to higher expected yields. (उचित समय पर सिंचाई — अधिक उपज)

 

• Water is essential for germination, photosynthesis, nutrient transport and cell turgidity; timely irrigation avoids both moisture stress and water-logging, both of which reduce yield.

 

• Modern efficient methods such as drip and sprinkler irrigation deliver water precisely and at the right time, improving water-use efficiency and crop output.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Critical stages for irrigation in most crops are the crown root initiation stage, tillering, flowering and grain-filling stages.

 

• Rabi crops (wheat, gram, mustard) are sown in winter and largely depend on irrigation, while Kharif crops (rice, maize, cotton) depend mainly on the monsoon.

 

• India's major irrigation sources are canals, wells/tube wells, tanks and, increasingly, micro-irrigation methods promoted under schemes like the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY).

 

NOTE

 

• Decreased nutrient uptake (Option A): Timely watering actually *increases* nutrient uptake by dissolving and transporting soil nutrients to roots.

 

• Increased vulnerability to pests (Option C): It is over-irrigation/water-logging, not optimally timed irrigation, that tends to increase pest and fungal problems.

 

• Delayed maturation (Option D): Adequate timely water supply generally supports normal or faster maturation, not delay.

question: Why is the plasma membrane called selectively permeable?
option_1: It allows only certain substances to pass in or out.
option_3: It allows all substances to pass freely.
option_4: It blocks all substances from entering.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It allows only certain substances to pass in or out.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The plasma membrane (cell membrane) is called selectively (semi) permeable because it allows only certain molecules — such as water, oxygen and carbon dioxide — to pass through freely, while regulating or blocking the movement of other substances. (चयनात्मक पारगम्यता — कुछ पदार्थों को ही आने-जाने देना)

 

• This selective control is essential for maintaining the cell's internal environment (homeostasis), allowing nutrients in and waste products out while keeping harmful substances at bay.

 

• The membrane follows the fluid mosaic model, proposed by Singer and Nicolson (1972), being made of a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins that act as channels and carriers for selective transport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Transport across the membrane occurs by diffusion, osmosis (passive, no energy required) and active transport (requires ATP, moves substances against their concentration gradient).

 

• Osmosis is the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water concentration to lower water concentration through a selectively permeable membrane.

 

• The plasma membrane is composed mainly of lipids (phospholipids) and proteins, along with some carbohydrates on the outer surface.

 

NOTE

 

• It dissolves unwanted materials (Option B): The membrane does not dissolve substances; it regulates their passage.

 

• It allows all substances to pass freely (Option C): This would describe a fully permeable membrane, not a selective one.

 

• It blocks all substances from entering (Option D): This would make the cell impermeable, preventing essential exchange needed for survival.

question: An electric bulb is rated 110 Watt – 220 Volt. The current drawn by the bulb is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.5 A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electric power P = V × I, where V is voltage and I is current, so I = P/V. (विद्युत शक्ति = वोल्टेज × धारा)

 

• Here P = 110 W and V = 220 V, so I = 110/220 = 0.5 A.

 

• The 'rating' of an appliance (e.g. 110 W–220 V) specifies the power it consumes when connected to its rated voltage; this determines the safe current it draws under normal operation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistance of the bulb can be found from R = V²/P = (220)²/110 = 440 Ω.

 

• Electrical energy consumed is measured commercially in kilowatt-hour (kWh or 'unit'): 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ joules.

 

• Ohm's Law: V = IR, applicable to devices with constant resistance (ohmic conductors) at constant temperature.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 A, 2 A (Options B, C): These would only result from arithmetic errors, e.g. dividing voltage by power instead of power by voltage.

 

• 24,200 A (Option D): This is the product V × P (220 × 110), not the current; multiplying instead of dividing gives a nonsensical, huge value for a small household bulb.

question: Which of the following is NOT a method of irrigation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Check dams.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Check dams are small barriers built across streams or drainage channels to slow down and store surface runoff, primarily for groundwater recharge and soil/water conservation, not as a direct method of delivering irrigation water to fields. (चेक डैम — भू-जल पुनर्भरण की संरचना, सिंचाई विधि नहीं)

 

• The main methods of irrigation used to actually supply water to crops are canals, wells/tube wells, tanks and river lift (river-lift pump) systems, along with modern methods like drip and sprinkler irrigation.

 

• A check dam instead acts as a water-harvesting structure: it raises the water table nearby, which farmers may later tap using wells — an indirect, not direct, irrigation role.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Canals are the most important source of irrigation in the northern plains of India (fed by perennial Himalayan rivers).

 

• Wells and tube wells are the largest source of irrigation in India overall, especially in the northwestern states.

 

• Tanks are important sources of irrigation in peninsular India, especially in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, due to undulating relief and impervious rocks.

 

NOTE

 

• River lift systems (Option A): Directly lift water from rivers using pumps to irrigate fields at higher elevations — a genuine irrigation method.

 

• Wells (Option B): A traditional and major direct source of irrigation water across India.

 

• Canals (Option D): Man-made channels that carry river/reservoir water directly to agricultural fields.

question: A man lifts a stone of mass 22 kg through a vertical height of 4 m. Calculate the work done. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 880 J.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Work done in lifting an object against gravity equals the gain in gravitational potential energy: W = mgh. (कार्य = भार × ऊँचाई)

 

• Here mass m = 22 kg, g = 10 m/s², height h = 4 m.

 

• W = 22 × 10 × 4 = 880 J.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Work is said to be done only when a force produces displacement in the direction of the force; W = F × d × cos θ.

 

• The SI unit of work and energy is the joule (J), equal to 1 newton-metre.

 

• Power is the rate of doing work: P = W/t, measured in watts.

 

NOTE

 

• 220 J (Option B): Obtained by using only the weight (mg = 220 N) without multiplying by the height.

 

• 400 J (Option C): Does not correspond to a straightforward calculation using the given values; likely a distractor from a miscalculation.

 

• 55 J (Option D): Results from dividing rather than correctly multiplying the given quantities.

question: A concave mirror forms an image at a distance of 20 cm when an object is placed 10 cm in front of it. What is the focal length of this mirror?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20 cm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Since the object distance (10 cm) here is less than the resulting focal length, the object lies within the focus, so the concave mirror forms a virtual, erect and magnified image behind the mirror — this is exactly how a concave mirror works as a shaving/make-up mirror. (अवतल दर्पण — फोकस के भीतर वस्तु होने पर आभासी, बड़ा प्रतिबिम्ब)

 

• Using the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u with the New Cartesian sign convention (distances measured against incident light are negative; a virtual image forms behind the mirror and is positive): object distance u = −10 cm, virtual image distance v = +20 cm.

 

• 1/f = 1/20 + 1/(−10) = 1/20 − 2/20 = −1/20, so f = −20 cm. The magnitude of the focal length is 20 cm (the negative sign simply confirms it is a concave mirror).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• For a concave mirror, if the object lies beyond the focus, a real, inverted image forms in front of the mirror; if it lies within the focus, a virtual, erect, magnified image forms behind the mirror.

 

• Radius of curvature R = 2f, so here R would be about 40 cm.

 

• A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image, regardless of object position, and is used as rear-view/side mirrors in vehicles.

 

NOTE

 

• 30 cm, 40 cm (Options A, C): Do not satisfy the mirror formula for the given object and image distances.

 

• 10 cm (Option B): Would be the case only if the image and object distances were equal (object at the centre of curvature), which is not so here.

question: Which of the following expressions is representing the correct lens formula?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The lens formula relates the object distance (u), image distance (v) and focal length (f) of a spherical lens: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. (लेंस सूत्र)

 

• It holds for both convex and concave lenses, following the New Cartesian sign convention where distances are measured from the optical centre, with distances against the direction of incident light taken as negative.

 

• This differs from the mirror formula (1/v + 1/u = 1/f) because for lenses, light passes through the lens (refraction on both sides), while for mirrors it reflects back on the same side.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Magnification for a lens: m = v/u = h'/h, where h' is image height and h is object height.

 

• Power of a lens P = 1/f (f in metres), measured in dioptres (D). Convex (converging) lenses have positive power; concave (diverging) lenses have negative power.

 

• The human eye behaves like a convex lens system, and its power can be adjusted by the ciliary muscles — a process called accommodation.

 

NOTE

 

• 1/v − 1/u = f (Option A): Incorrect — this equates the difference of reciprocals to f, not 1/f.

 

• 1/v + 1/u = f (Option C): Incorrect for the same reason and also uses '+' which applies to mirrors, not lenses.

 

• 1/v + 1/u = 1/f (Option D): This is the correct mirror formula, not the lens formula.

question: Why do we experience muscle cramps after heavy exercise?
option_1: Due to accumulation of lactic acid
option_2: Due to a decrease in body temperature
option_4: Because blood flow completely stops during exercise
solution_text:
The correct answer is Due to accumulation of lactic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During heavy/vigorous exercise, the muscles' demand for oxygen exceeds supply, so muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration, breaking down glucose into lactic acid instead of fully oxidising it. (लैक्टिक अम्ल संचय — पेशी ऐंठन)

 

• Accumulation of lactic acid in the muscle tissue causes fatigue, soreness and painful muscle cramps.

 

• Anaerobic respiration in muscles: Glucose → Lactic acid + Energy (a much smaller amount of energy than aerobic respiration, since the process is incomplete).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aerobic respiration (in presence of oxygen): Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + Energy (38 ATP), which is far more efficient than anaerobic respiration (2 ATP).

 

• In yeast, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) produces ethanol and CO₂ instead of lactic acid — used in the baking and brewing industries.

 

• Rest and stretching help clear accumulated lactic acid from muscles by restoring normal oxygen supply (allowing it to be converted back to glucose/broken down in the liver).

 

NOTE

 

• Due to a decrease in body temperature (Option B): Exercise typically raises, not lowers, body temperature.

 

• Because muscles stop contracting (Option C): Cramps are actually caused by sustained, involuntary contraction, not the stopping of contraction.

 

• Because blood flow completely stops during exercise (Option D): Blood flow to muscles actually *increases* during exercise; it does not stop.

question: What is the IUPAC name for an organic compound with two carbon atoms and a hydroxyl (–OH) functional group?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A compound with two carbon atoms and a hydroxyl (–OH) group attached to a saturated carbon chain is an alcohol with the formula C₂H₅OH, whose IUPAC name is Ethanol. (एथेनॉल — दो कार्बन परमाणु व हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह)

 

• IUPAC naming of alcohols uses the suffix '-ol' added to the name of the corresponding alkane: 'eth-' (2 carbons) + '-ol' = Ethanol.

 

• Ethanol is the active intoxicating ingredient found in alcoholic beverages and is also used as a solvent, in sanitisers and, increasingly, as a biofuel (blended with petrol as 'ethanol blending' in India, e.g. E20 fuel).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alcohols contain the functional group –OH; carboxylic acids contain –COOH; aldehydes contain –CHO; ketones contain >C=O (between two carbons).

 

• Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to release hydrogen gas: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂↑.

 

• On oxidation, ethanol can be converted to ethanoic acid (acetic acid, CH₃COOH) — the process used commercially to make vinegar.

 

NOTE

 

• Propanone (Option A): A ketone (CH₃COCH₃, commonly acetone) with three carbon atoms and a >C=O group, not –OH.

 

• Ethanoic acid (Option B): A carboxylic acid (CH₃COOH) with the –COOH functional group, not a simple hydroxyl group.

 

• Methanal (Option C): An aldehyde (HCHO, formaldehyde) with only one carbon atom and a –CHO group.

question: Which statement correctly represents the location of the meristematic tissue in a plant body?
option_3: At the base of the stem
option_4: At the tips of the leaves
solution_text:
The correct answer is At the base of the stem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Meristematic tissue is found only at specific growing regions of a plant — the root tip, shoot tip (apical meristem) and, in many plants, at nodes and the base of the stem/leaves (intercalary meristem). Among the given options, 'at the base of the stem' correctly identifies one such specific meristematic region. (विभज्योतक ऊतक — विशिष्ट वृद्धि क्षेत्रों में)

 

• Cells of meristematic tissue are living, thin-walled, with dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei, and they actively divide by mitosis to add new cells, which later differentiate into permanent tissues.

 

• Intercalary meristem, found at the base of leaves or internodes (typical of grasses), allows for regrowth after grazing or mowing — this is why grass keeps growing back after cutting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Apical meristem: present at the tips of roots and shoots; responsible for increase in the length of the plant (primary growth).

 

• Lateral meristem (e.g. vascular cambium, cork cambium): present along the sides of stems and roots; responsible for increase in girth/thickness (secondary growth).

 

• Permanent tissue is formed from meristematic tissue once cells lose the ability to divide and become specialised for a fixed function (e.g. parenchyma, xylem, phloem).

 

NOTE

 

• All over the plant body (Option A): Incorrect — meristematic tissue is restricted to specific growing points, not distributed throughout the plant.

 

• At some specific regions (Option B): Though generally true, it is a vague, non-specific statement compared to the precisely correct location named in Option C.

 

• At the tips of the leaves (Option D): Leaf tips are not a primary meristematic zone; leaf growth mainly occurs via marginal or basal meristems, not the tip.

question: Which of the following reproductive method will generate greater diversity in population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sexual reproduction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of male and female gametes from two different parents, causing genetic material (DNA) to mix and recombine, producing offspring with new combinations of traits — hence generating much greater genetic diversity. (लैंगिक प्रजनन — अधिक आनुवंशिक विविधता)

 

• This diversity is advantageous for a species' ability to survive changing environments and evolve over time, since a genetically varied population is more likely to have some individuals suited to new conditions.

 

• In contrast, asexual reproduction methods (binary fission, budding, fragmentation) involve only one parent, so offspring are genetically identical clones of the parent, offering little to no variation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Binary fission: a single-celled organism (e.g. Amoeba, bacteria) splits into two identical daughter cells.

 

• Budding: a new individual develops as an outgrowth (bud) from the parent body and eventually detaches (e.g. Hydra, yeast).

 

• Fragmentation: the parent body breaks into pieces, each of which grows into a new individual (e.g. Spirogyra, planaria).

 

NOTE

 

• Binary fission (Option B): Produces genetically identical offspring; no genetic mixing occurs.

 

• Budding (Option C): Also asexual; the bud is genetically identical to the parent.

 

• Fragmentation (Option D): Similarly asexual, producing clones with no new genetic combinations.

question: When an empty plastic bottle with an airtight stopper is pushed deeper into a bucket of water, the increasing upward force that resists the downward push is known as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buoyant force (or upthrust).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The upward force exerted by a fluid (liquid or gas) on a body submerged (partially or fully) in it is called buoyant force or upthrust. (उत्प्लावन बल — तरल द्वारा ऊपर की ओर लगने वाला बल)

 

• As the airtight bottle is pushed deeper, it displaces more water; by Archimedes' Principle, the upthrust equals the weight of the water displaced, so pushing it deeper increases the volume of water displaced and hence the upward resisting force.

 

• This is the same force that makes objects feel lighter in water and allows ships, boats and swimmers to float.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Archimedes' Principle: when a body is partially or fully immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.

 

• An object floats if its average density is less than that of the fluid, and sinks if greater; it remains suspended if densities are equal.

 

• The buoyant force depends on the density of the fluid and the volume of fluid displaced, not on the mass or shape of the submerged object alone.

 

NOTE

 

• Gravitational force (Option A): Acts downward (pulling the bottle down), not as an upward resisting force.

 

• Surface tension (Option B): A property of the liquid surface that resists penetration at the surface; not the main increasing resistive force as depth increases.

 

• Atmospheric pressure (Option C): Acts on the water surface from above and is not the force directly resisting a bottle being pushed deeper underwater.

question: Detergents can work in which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both hard and soft water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Detergents are ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain carboxylic acids that form soluble products (a stable lather) with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water, unlike ordinary soap. (डिटर्जेंट — कठोर व मृदु दोनों जल में प्रभावी)

 

• Since detergents do not form an insoluble scum with Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ ions (unlike soap), they clean effectively in both hard and soft water.

 

• This is why detergents (used in washing powders, shampoos, dish-washing liquids) are widely preferred over ordinary soap in regions with hard water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Soap is a sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain fatty (carboxylic) acid, made by the process of saponification (hydrolysis of fats/oils with NaOH).

 

• In hard water, soap reacts with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions to form an insoluble scum, wasting soap and reducing lathering efficiency.

 

• Hard water contains dissolved calcium and magnesium bicarbonates/sulphates/chlorides; it can be softened by boiling (temporary hardness) or using methods like ion exchange (permanent hardness).

 

NOTE

 

• Only distilled water (Option B): Too restrictive — detergents work well in ordinary hard and soft water too, not just pure distilled water.

 

• Only soft water (Option C): Incorrect — the key advantage of detergents over soap is that they work even in hard water.

 

• Only hot water (Option D): Detergents are effective in both hot and cold water; temperature is not the limiting factor being tested here.

question: If the direction of current in a conductor is reversed, the direction of force on it will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is reverse.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force whose direction is given by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, and this direction depends on both the direction of current and the magnetic field. (फ्लेमिंग का बायाँ हाथ नियम)

 

• If the direction of current is reversed (while the magnetic field direction stays the same), the force F = IL × B also reverses direction, since force is proportional to the vector direction of current flow.

 

• This principle is used in electric motors, where periodically reversing the current (using a split-ring commutator in a DC motor) reverses the force on the coil, keeping it rotating continuously in one direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: if the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand are mutually perpendicular, with the forefinger pointing in the direction of the field and the middle finger in the direction of current, the thumb gives the direction of force.

 

• The magnitude of the force is given by F = BIL sin θ, where B is magnetic field strength, I is current, L is conductor length, and θ is the angle between current and field.

 

• Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is used instead for finding the direction of induced current in a generator (electromagnetic induction), not force on a current-carrying conductor.

 

NOTE

 

• Double (Option A): Reversing current changes the force's direction only, not its magnitude — the magnitude stays the same (assuming current magnitude is unchanged).

 

• Remain the same (Option B): Incorrect, since reversing current does reverse the direction of the force.

 

• Become zero (Option D): The force becomes zero only if the current is zero or parallel to the field, not simply upon reversing its direction.

question: Which of the following observations could NOT be explained by Rutherford's model of the atom?
option_1: The presence of a positively charged nucleus in the atom
option_2: The distribution of electrons around the nucleus
option_3: The deflection of alpha particles at large angles
option_4: The stability of the atom despite the presence of accelerating electrons
solution_text:
The correct answer is The stability of the atom despite the presence of accelerating electrons.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rutherford's atomic model (based on his alpha-particle scattering experiment) established that an atom has a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus at its centre, with electrons revolving around it in orbits — but it could not explain the stability of the atom. (रदरफोर्ड मॉडल — परमाणु की स्थिरता की व्याख्या नहीं कर सका)

 

• According to classical electromagnetic theory, an accelerating (revolving) charged particle like the electron should continuously radiate energy, causing it to spiral inward and collapse into the nucleus within a fraction of a second. Since atoms are, in reality, stable, this was a fundamental flaw of Rutherford's model.

 

• This limitation was later resolved by Niels Bohr (1913), who proposed that electrons revolve only in certain fixed, stable orbits (energy levels) without radiating energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rutherford's gold foil (alpha-particle scattering) experiment showed: (i) most alpha particles passed straight through the foil (atom is mostly empty space); (ii) a few were deflected at large angles, and a very few bounced straight back (indicating a small, dense, positively charged nucleus).

 

• Rutherford's model is also called the 'planetary' or 'nuclear' model of the atom, since electrons orbit the nucleus much like planets orbit the sun.

 

• Bohr's model introduced the idea of quantised energy levels (shells), correctly explaining atomic stability and atomic spectra.

 

NOTE

 

• The presence of a positively charged nucleus (Option A): Correctly explained and, in fact, discovered by Rutherford's experiment.

 

• The distribution of electrons around the nucleus (Option B): Rutherford's model did account for electrons revolving around the nucleus, even though it could not explain their stability.

 

• The deflection of alpha particles at large angles (Option C): This was precisely the key observation Rutherford's model successfully explained, leading to the discovery of the nucleus.

question: The nature of the bond formed in aliphatic carbon compounds is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is covalent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carbon has 4 valence electrons and forms bonds mainly by sharing electrons with other atoms (carbon or other elements like H, O, N, halogens) to complete its octet, resulting in covalent bonds. (सहसंयोजक बंधन — इलेक्ट्रॉनों की साझेदारी)

 

• Aliphatic compounds (open-chain, non-aromatic organic compounds such as alkanes, alkenes and alkynes) are formed almost entirely through single, double or triple covalent bonds between carbon atoms and/or with hydrogen and other elements.

 

• Because carbon compounds are held together by covalent bonds (rather than ionic bonds), they typically have low melting and boiling points, are generally poor conductors of electricity, and are often soluble in organic solvents rather than water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Catenation is carbon's unique ability to form long chains and rings by bonding with other carbon atoms — this, along with tetravalency, gives rise to the enormous diversity of organic compounds.

 

• Single, double and triple covalent bonds correspond to alkanes (C–C), alkenes (C=C) and alkynes (C≡C) respectively.

 

• Isomerism — compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures — is common in carbon compounds due to the versatility of covalent bonding.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen bond (Option A): A weak intermolecular force of attraction (e.g. between water molecules), not the primary bond within carbon compounds.

 

• Ionic (Option C): Formed by the complete transfer of electrons between a metal and a non-metal (e.g. NaCl); carbon, having 4 valence electrons, cannot easily lose or gain electrons to form stable ions.

 

• Coordinate (Option D): A special type of covalent bond in which both shared electrons come from one atom; not the typical bond type in ordinary aliphatic hydrocarbons.

question:
Read the given Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and select the correct option.

(A): Mendel chose pea plants for his experiments because they were easy to grow and showed distinct contrasting traits.

(R): Pea plants reproduce asexually, allowing Mendel to control crosses easily.
option_1: A is true, but R is false
option_2: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_3: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true, but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true: Gregor Mendel chose the garden pea (Pisum sativum) for his hybridisation experiments because it is easy to grow, has a short life cycle, and shows several distinct, contrasting (either-or) traits — such as tall/dwarf, round/wrinkled seeds, and green/yellow pods. (मेंडल — मटर के पौधे पर प्रयोग)

 

• Reason (R) is false: Pea plants are naturally self-pollinating (a form of sexual reproduction), not asexually reproducing. This self-pollinating nature actually allowed Mendel to obtain pure-breeding (true-breeding) lines, and he could artificially cross-pollinate selected plants by hand (emasculation and dusting pollen) to control crosses precisely.

 

• Since R makes a factually incorrect claim (that pea plants reproduce asexually), it cannot be a correct explanation of A, even though A itself is true.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendel proposed the Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation and Law of Independent Assortment based on his pea plant experiments (1856–1863), laying the foundation of modern genetics.

 

• He studied seven pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants: seed shape, seed colour, flower colour, pod shape, pod colour, flower position and stem height.

 

• Mendel's work was largely ignored during his lifetime and was rediscovered independently around 1900 by de Vries, Correns and Tschermak.

 

NOTE

 

• Options B and C are incorrect because Reason (R) is factually false — pea plants reproduce sexually (via self-pollination), not asexually.

 

• Option D is incorrect because Assertion (A) is a true and well-established historical/scientific fact about Mendel's choice of pea plants.

question: When dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate, which of the following observations is correct?
option_1: Formation of a salt and water only
option_2: Rapid evolution of a colourless gas that turns lime water milky
option_3: Formation of brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide
option_4: Formation of hydrogen gas with a pop sound
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rapid evolution of a colourless gas that turns lime water milky.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃, baking soda) reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce sodium chloride, water and carbon dioxide gas: NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑. (सोडियम हाइड्रोजनकार्बोनेट + तनु HCl → कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड गैस)

 

• The carbon dioxide gas evolves rapidly with brisk effervescence and is colourless; when passed into lime water (calcium hydroxide solution), it turns the lime water milky due to formation of insoluble calcium carbonate — the standard confirmatory test for CO₂.

 

• This is a classic acid–bicarbonate reaction, similar to that of metal carbonates with acids, and is the basis of the fizz produced when antacids (containing bicarbonates) are taken to relieve acidity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Baking soda (NaHCO₃) is used in cooking (as a leavening/raising agent, releasing CO₂ to make dough rise), in fire extinguishers, and as a mild antacid.

 

• On heating, NaHCO₃ decomposes to give sodium carbonate, water and CO₂: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂.

 

• Testing for CO₂ using lime water: excess CO₂ eventually makes the milky solution clear again due to the formation of soluble calcium bicarbonate.

 

NOTE

 

• Formation of a salt and water only (Option A): Incomplete — the reaction also releases carbon dioxide gas, which is the most easily observable feature of the reaction.

 

• Formation of brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide (Option C): NO₂ fumes result from reactions involving nitrates/nitric acid, not from a carbonate/bicarbonate with HCl.

 

• Formation of hydrogen gas with a pop sound (Option D): Hydrogen gas is released when a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid, not from a hydrogencarbonate reacting with an acid.

question: Suspensions are different from solutions because:
option_1: They can be seen by naked eyes
option_4: Their particles do not settle on standing
solution_text:
The correct answer is They can be seen by naked eyes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which solute particles are large enough (usually >1000 nm) to remain visible to the naked eye and do not dissolve completely, unlike a true solution, which is homogeneous with particles too small to be seen. (निलंबन — नग्न आँखों से दिखाई देने वाले कण)

 

• Particles of a suspension scatter light (show the Tyndall effect), appear cloudy/opaque, and tend to settle down on standing due to gravity — none of which happens in a true solution.

 

• Common examples of suspensions: muddy/chalky water, paint. Common examples of solutions: salt or sugar dissolved in water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Colloids (e.g. milk, fog, smoke) lie between solutions and suspensions in particle size (1–1000 nm); their particles do not settle and they also show the Tyndall effect, but cannot be separated by simple filtration (unlike suspensions).

 

• Suspension particles can be separated by filtration, whereas solute particles of a true solution cannot be separated by filtration.

 

• A true solution is always transparent and does not scatter light (no Tyndall effect), and its particles never settle on standing.

 

NOTE

 

• Their solute is fully dissolved (Option B): This describes a solution, not a suspension — in a suspension, particles remain undissolved.

 

• They are transparent (Option C): Suspensions are typically cloudy/opaque, not transparent — transparency is a property of true solutions.

 

• Their particles do not settle on standing (Option D): Incorrect — a defining feature of suspensions is that particles *do* settle on standing, unlike true solutions or stable colloids.

question: If an object moves from point A to point B (50 m east) and returns to point A in 10 seconds, its average velocity is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0 m/s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Average velocity = total displacement / total time, where displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between the initial and final positions, along with direction. (औसत वेग = कुल विस्थापन / कुल समय)

 

• Since the object starts at point A and, after moving to B and back, ends up again at point A, its net displacement is zero (the object returns to its starting position).

 

• Therefore, average velocity = 0 / 10 = 0 m/s, regardless of the actual path length (100 m total) covered or the time taken.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Average speed, by contrast, = total distance / total time = (50 + 50)/10 = 10 m/s; speed and velocity can differ significantly when the object returns to its starting point.

 

• Distance is a scalar quantity (only magnitude), while displacement is a vector quantity (magnitude and direction).

 

• Average velocity can be zero even if the object was moving throughout the journey — velocity measures net change of position, not motion itself.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 m/s (Option A): This would be roughly half of the average speed value, not the average velocity, and does not correspond to any correct calculation here.

 

• −10 m/s (Option C): This resembles the (negative) average velocity of just the return leg alone (B to A), not the entire round trip.

 

• 10 m/s (Option D): This is actually the average speed for the whole trip, not the average velocity, which is zero due to zero net displacement.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct about molecular mass?

Statement 1: The molecular mass of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule of the substance.

Statement 2: It is also known as the relative mass of a molecule.

Statement 3: It is expressed in atomic mass units (u).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements about molecular mass are correct. (आणविक द्रव्यमान — सभी कथन सही)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: The molecular mass of a substance is defined as the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in one molecule of that substance. For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) = 2(1) + 16 = 18 u.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Molecular mass is also called the relative molecular mass, since it expresses how many times a molecule is heavier than 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom (the reference standard).

 

• Statement 3 is correct: Molecular mass is expressed in atomic mass units (u), also called daltons (Da); 1 u is defined as exactly 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Formula unit mass is used for ionic compounds (e.g. NaCl) that do not exist as discrete molecules, calculated the same way as molecular mass by summing the masses of the constituent ions/atoms in the formula unit.

 

• Mole concept: one mole of any substance contains 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number) and has a mass equal to its molecular/atomic mass expressed in grams (molar mass).

 

• Gram molecular mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, numerically equal to its molecular mass but expressed in grams.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, C and D are incorrect because each of them wrongly excludes at least one statement, whereas Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all independently correct and standard definitions of molecular mass.

question: A typist takes 40 minutes to type 2 pages. How long (in minutes) will he take to type 87 pages?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 1740.

 

GIVEN

 

• Time to type 2 pages = 40 minutes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time per page = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 minutes/page.

 

• Time for 87 pages = 87 × 20 = 1740 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Directly scale up: (87/2) × 40 = 43.5 × 40 = 1740.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the unit rate (time per page) first, then multiply by the required quantity.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 9 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 36 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 6.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills tank in 9 min. Emptying pipe: empties full tank in 36 min. Both opened together on an empty tank.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Combined rate = 1/9 − 1/36 = (4 − 1)/36 = 3/36 = 1/12 of the tank per minute.

 

• Time to fill the full tank = 12 minutes.

 

• Time to fill half the tank = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• LCM method: take tank capacity = LCM(9,36) = 36 units. Fill rate = 4 units/min, empty rate = 1 unit/min, net = 3 units/min. Half tank = 18 units ÷ 3 = 6 min.

 

NOTE

 

• When two pipes work in opposite directions (fill vs empty), subtract their rates to get the net rate.

question: Divide ₹8,118 between Ravina and Sarita in the ratio 3 : 15, then find the share of Sarita.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹6,765.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total amount = ₹8,118, to be divided between Ravina and Sarita in ratio 3 : 15.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Ratio 3 : 15 simplifies to 1 : 5 (dividing both by 3); total parts = 1 + 5 = 6.

 

• Value of 1 part = 8118 ÷ 6 = ₹1,353.

 

• Sarita's share (5 parts) = 5 × 1,353 = ₹6,765.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Sarita's share = [15/(3+15)] × 8118 = (15/18) × 8118 = (5/6) × 8118 = 6765.

 

NOTE

 

• Always simplify the ratio first — it makes the division into parts much easier.

question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7.5% per annum, respectively. Chetan borrowed an amount of ₹2,00,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Chetan after 3 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 24,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal = ₹2,00,000 from each bank; Rate A = 3.5% p.a., Rate B = 7.5% p.a.; Time = 3 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• SI = (P × R × T)/100.

 

• SI from Bank A = (2,00,000 × 3.5 × 3)/100 = ₹21,000.

 

• SI from Bank B = (2,00,000 × 7.5 × 3)/100 = ₹45,000.

 

• Positive difference = 45,000 − 21,000 = ₹24,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since principal and time are common, difference = P × T × (R₂ − R₁)/100 = 2,00,000 × 3 × (7.5 − 3.5)/100 = 2,00,000 × 3 × 4/100 = ₹24,000.

 

NOTE

 

• When principal and time are the same for two rates, you can directly use the *difference of rates* to save calculation time.

question: A can complete a piece of work in 90 days. B is 75% less efficient than A. C is 80% more efficient than B. If B and C work together for 30 days, A alone will complete the remaining work in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 69 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• A completes the work in 90 days. B is 75% less efficient than A. C is 80% more efficient than B.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let A's efficiency = 1 unit/day, so total work = 90 × 1 = 90 units.

 

• B's efficiency = 1 × (1 − 0.75) = 0.25 units/day.

 

• C's efficiency = 0.25 × (1 + 0.80) = 0.25 × 1.8 = 0.45 units/day.

 

• (B + C)'s combined efficiency = 0.25 + 0.45 = 0.7 units/day.

 

• Work done by B and C in 30 days = 30 × 0.7 = 21 units.

 

• Remaining work = 90 − 21 = 69 units; A alone (at 1 unit/day) takes 69 ÷ 1 = 69 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take A's efficiency = 100. Then B = 25, C = 25 × 1.8 = 45. Total work = 100 × 90 = 9000. (B+C) in 30 days = 30 × 70 = 2100. Remaining = 9000 − 2100 = 6900; A's days = 6900/100 = 69.

 

NOTE

 

• 'X% less efficient than A' means efficiency = A's efficiency × (1 − X/100); 'X% more efficient' means × (1 + X/100).

question: After selling an article at a discount of 44%, the profit percentage obtained is 12%. What is the markup percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 100%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount offered = 44%; resulting profit = 12% (over cost price).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let cost price (CP) = 100. Since profit = 12%, selling price (SP) = 112.

 

• Let marked price (MP) = M. Since discount = 44%, SP = M × (1 − 0.44) = 0.56M.

 

• 0.56M = 112 ⇒ M = 112/0.56 = 200.

 

• Markup % = [(MP − CP)/CP] × 100 = [(200 − 100)/100] × 100 = 100%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• MP/CP = (100 + profit%)/(100 − discount%) = 112/56 = 2, so MP is 200% of CP, i.e. markup = (2 − 1) × 100 = 100%.

 

NOTE

 

• Markup % = [(MP − CP)/CP] × 100; it is calculated on cost price, not on marked price.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 96, then the result is the same number. 70% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 84.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number N, when added to 96, equals N itself.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 96 + 0.2N = N ⇒ 96 = N − 0.2N = 0.8N ⇒ N = 96/0.8 = 120.

 

• 70% of N = 0.7 × 120 = 84.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 96 corresponds to 80% of N (since 100% − 20% = 80%), so N = 96 × (100/80) = 120; then 70% of 120 = 84.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert 'X added gives the same number' statements into an equation with the unknown on both sides, then simplify.

question: If a – b = 6 and ab = 135, then find a possible value of (a + b).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 24.

 

GIVEN

 

• a − b = 6, ab = 135.

 

SOLUTION

 

• (a + b)² = (a − b)² + 4ab = 6² + 4 × 135 = 36 + 540 = 576.

 

• a + b = √576 = 24 (taking the positive value).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Directly use the identity (a+b)² = (a−b)² + 4ab whenever a−b and ab are given — avoids solving a quadratic for a and b individually.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember both key identities: (a+b)² = (a−b)² + 4ab and (a−b)² = (a+b)² − 4ab.

question: The volume of a right circular cylinder is 13,860 cm³ and the circumference of its base is 66 cm. The height of this cylinder is: (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 40 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Volume = 13,860 cm³; circumference of base = 66 cm; π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Circumference = 2πr ⇒ 66 = 2 × (22/7) × r ⇒ r = 66 × 7/44 = 10.5 cm.

 

• Base area = πr² = (22/7) × (10.5)² = (22/7) × 110.25 = 346.5 cm².

 

• Volume = Base area × height ⇒ 13,860 = 346.5 × h ⇒ h = 13,860 / 346.5 = 40 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First find r from circumference (r = C/2π), then use h = Volume/(πr²) directly in one line without separately restating the base area.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of a cylinder = πr²h; always extract the radius from the circumference before computing volume-related quantities.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 16% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 80% and that of the TV decreases by 44%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 5 washing machines and 2 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Increase by 40%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine cost is 16% less than TV cost. Washing machine cost increases by 80%; TV cost decreases by 44%. Compare total cost of 5 washing machines + 2 TVs, before and after.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = 100, so washing machine cost = 100 × (1 − 0.16) = 84.

 

• Old total = 5 × 84 + 2 × 100 = 420 + 200 = 620.

 

• New washing machine cost = 84 × 1.80 = 151.2; new TV cost = 100 × 0.56 = 56.

 

• New total = 5 × 151.2 + 2 × 56 = 756 + 112 = 868.

 

• % change = [(868 − 620)/620] × 100 = (248/620) × 100 = 40% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume convenient base values (TV = 100) from the start so that all further percentage operations become simple whole-number arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• When multiple percentage changes are combined across different quantities, always work with actual total values (not just percentages) to avoid errors.

question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 9 cm is melted and recast into smaller spherical balls, each of radius 3 cm. Find the number of such small balls formed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 27.

 

GIVEN

 

• Radius of large sphere = 9 cm; radius of each small sphere = 3 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since volume is conserved on melting and recasting, Number of balls = Volume of large sphere ÷ Volume of one small sphere = (4/3)π(9)³ ÷ (4/3)π(3)³ = (9/3)³ = 3³ = 27.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Number of smaller identical spheres formed = (R/r)³, where R and r are the radii of the big and small spheres. Here (9/3)³ = 27.

 

NOTE

 

• This cube-of-ratio shortcut works because volume scales with the cube of linear dimensions.

question: The present age of Mohan is three times the age of his son Rakesh. Four years ago from now, Mohan's age was four times his son's age at that time. What will be Rakesh's age (in years) after 7 years from now?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 19.

 

GIVEN

 

• Present: Mohan's age = 3 × Rakesh's age. 4 years ago: Mohan's age = 4 × Rakesh's age (at that time).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Rakesh's present age = R, so Mohan's present age = 3R.

 

• 4 years ago: Mohan = 3R − 4, Rakesh = R − 4. Given: 3R − 4 = 4(R − 4).

 

• 3R − 4 = 4R − 16 ⇒ 16 − 4 = 4R − 3R ⇒ R = 12.

 

• Rakesh's age after 7 years = 12 + 7 = 19.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up the two age equations directly in terms of one variable (Rakesh's present age) — age problems almost always reduce to a simple linear equation this way.

 

NOTE

 

• Always be careful to apply the same number of years (here, 4 years ago) to BOTH people's ages before writing the ratio/equation.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 2/90?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 225%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find what percentage 1/20 is of 2/90.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Required % = (1/20) ÷ (2/90) × 100 = (1/20) × (90/2) × 100.

 

• = (90/40) × 100 = 2.25 × 100 = 225%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'A is what % of B' = (A/B) × 100; convert both fractions to decimals first if that's quicker: 1/20 = 0.05, 2/90 ≈ 0.0222; 0.05/0.0222 × 100 ≈ 225%.

 

NOTE

 

• Always divide the 'is' value by the 'of' value, not the other way round, when finding percentages.

question: A garrison of 1200 men has provisions for 12 days. How long (in days) will the provisions last if the garrison be increased by 600 men?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 8.

 

GIVEN

 

• 1200 men have provisions for 12 days; garrison increased by 600 men (new total = 1800 men).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total provisions = 1200 × 12 = 14,400 man-days (a fixed quantity).

 

• New number of days = 14,400 ÷ 1800 = 8 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use inverse proportion directly: New days = Old days × (Old men / New men) = 12 × (1200/1800) = 12 × 2/3 = 8.

 

NOTE

 

• More men consuming the same total provisions means fewer days — men and days are inversely proportional here.

question: By selling 20 pens for the cost price of 25 pens, what is the profit percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 25%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling price of 20 pens = Cost price of 25 pens.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let cost price of 1 pen = ₹1. Then CP of 25 pens = ₹25 = SP of 20 pens.

 

• CP of 20 pens = ₹20. Profit (on 20 pens) = SP − CP = 25 − 20 = ₹5.

 

• Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (5/20) × 100 = 25%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When SP of 'x' articles = CP of 'y' articles (y > x), Profit % = [(y − x)/x] × 100 = [(25 − 20)/20] × 100 = 25%.

 

NOTE

 

• This 'selling fewer for the cost of more' setup always represents a profit; the shortcut formula saves assuming cost price values manually.

question: If a 2622 m long train crosses a pole in 57 seconds, then find the time (in seconds) taken by the train to cross a 736 m long platform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 73.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = 2622 m; crosses a pole (negligible length) in 57 s; platform length = 736 m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Speed of train = distance/time = 2622/57 = 46 m/s (crossing a pole means covering only its own length).

 

• To cross the platform, total distance = train length + platform length = 2622 + 736 = 3358 m.

 

• Time = distance/speed = 3358/46 = 73 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Extra time due to platform = platform length ÷ speed = 736/46 = 16 s; total time = 57 + 16 = 73 s.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Crossing a pole/man' means the train covers only its own length; 'crossing a platform' means it covers (train length + platform length).

question: If 2ˣ = 8 and 3ʸ = 27, find the value of (2ˣ⁺¹ × 3ʸ⁻²).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 48.

 

GIVEN

 

• 2ˣ = 8 and 3ʸ = 27.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 2ˣ = 8 = 2³ ⇒ x = 3. 3ʸ = 27 = 3³ ⇒ y = 3.

 

• 2ˣ⁺¹ × 3ʸ⁻² = 2⁴ × 3¹ = 16 × 3 = 48.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each equation to the same base first (8 = 2³, 27 = 3³) to instantly read off x and y, then substitute directly into the expression.

 

NOTE

 

• When bases match on both sides of an equation like aᵐ = aⁿ, simply equate the exponents (m = n).

question: Bharat buys a gold ring for his mother. The ring is marked at ₹96,000 and is offered with two successive discounts of 25% and Q%, respectively. After receiving both discounts, he pays ₹18,000. Find the value of Q.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 75.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = ₹96,000; successive discounts of 25% and Q%; final price paid = ₹18,000.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After the first discount of 25%: Price = 96,000 × (1 − 0.25) = 96,000 × 0.75 = ₹72,000.

 

• After the second discount of Q%: 72,000 × (1 − Q/100) = 18,000.

 

• (1 − Q/100) = 18,000/72,000 = 0.25 ⇒ Q/100 = 0.75 ⇒ Q = 75.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combined single discount needed = (96,000 − 18,000)/96,000 × 100 = 81.25%. Using the successive-discount formula, 25 + Q − (25×Q)/100 = 81.25, solving gives Q = 75.

 

NOTE

 

• Apply successive discounts one after another on the reduced price, not by simply adding the two percentages.

question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first person walks at 10.8 km/hr, and the second person walks at 21.6 km/hr. The train takes 15 seconds and 20 seconds, respectively, to completely pass them. What is the speed of the train if both persons are walking in the same direction as the train?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 54 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Person 1 walks at 10.8 km/hr, train overtakes in 15 s. Person 2 walks at 21.6 km/hr, train overtakes in 20 s. Both walk in the same direction as the train.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert speeds to m/s: 10.8 km/hr = 10.8 × 5/18 = 3 m/s; 21.6 km/hr = 21.6 × 5/18 = 6 m/s.

 

• Let train speed = v m/s and train length = L m. Same direction ⇒ relative speed = (v − walking speed).

 

• Overtaking Person 1: L = 15 × (v − 3). Overtaking Person 2: L = 20 × (v − 6).

 

• 15(v − 3) = 20(v − 6) ⇒ 15v − 45 = 20v − 120 ⇒ 120 − 45 = 20v − 15v ⇒ 75 = 5v ⇒ v = 15 m/s.

 

• Speed in km/hr = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up L = t(v − u) for each person, eliminate L by equating the two expressions, and solve the resulting linear equation for v.

 

NOTE

 

• For 'overtaking' (same direction), relative speed = difference of speeds; for 'crossing' (opposite direction), relative speed = sum of speeds.

question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 3 cm more than twice the breadth. Find the breadth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 8 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Perimeter = 54 cm; length = 2 × breadth + 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let breadth = b, so length L = 2b + 3.

 

• Perimeter = 2(L + b) = 54 ⇒ L + b = 27.

 

• (2b + 3) + b = 27 ⇒ 3b + 3 = 27 ⇒ 3b = 24 ⇒ b = 8 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Directly substitute L = 2b+3 into (L+b) = Perimeter/2, reducing the problem to one simple linear equation in b.

 

NOTE

 

• Perimeter of rectangle = 2(length + breadth); always use half the perimeter (here 27) to simplify further steps.

question: A 20-metre-tall building has an observer at the top looking at a point on the ground. If the line of sight to that point makes a downward-facing angle of 45°, what is the horizontal distance from the building's base to that point?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 20 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Height of building = 20 m; angle of depression from top to the point on ground = 45°.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let horizontal distance from the base to the point = d. The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the point to the top (alternate angles), so tan 45° = height/d.

 

• tan 45° = 1 = 20/d ⇒ d = 20 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the angle of elevation/depression is 45°, the horizontal distance always equals the height (since tan 45° = 1) — no need for a full calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Angle of depression (measured from the observer looking down) is always equal to the angle of elevation (measured from the object looking up) between the same two points.

question:
Find the median of the given data, if the cumulative frequency is 45.

Class Interval: 1-11, 11-21, 21-31, 31-41

Frequency: 10, 11, X, 11
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 22 2/13.

 

GIVEN

 

• Class intervals 1-11, 11-21, 21-31, 31-41 with frequencies 10, 11, X, 11; total cumulative frequency (n) = 45.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of frequencies = 10 + 11 + X + 11 = 45 ⇒ X = 13.

 

• Cumulative frequencies: up to 11 → 10; up to 21 → 21; up to 31 → 21+13 = 34; up to 41 → 34+11 = 45.

 

• n/2 = 45/2 = 22.5, which lies in the cumulative frequency 34 (class 21-31), so the median class is 21-31.

 

• Median = L + [(n/2 − CF)/f] × h, where L = 21 (lower limit), CF = 21 (cumulative frequency before median class), f = 13, h = 10.

 

• Median = 21 + [(22.5 − 21)/13] × 10 = 21 + (1.5 × 10)/13 = 21 + 15/13 = 21 + 1 2/13 = 22 2/13.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First determine the missing frequency using the total, then locate the median class by comparing n/2 against the cumulative frequency column before applying the median formula.

 

NOTE

 

• The median class is the one whose cumulative frequency first equals or exceeds n/2; don't confuse CF (before the median class) with the median class's own cumulative frequency.

question: Akshat and Neha together invested ₹57,000 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹8,000, Akshat's share was ₹2,200. How much was Akshat's investment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹15,675.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment = ₹57,000; total profit = ₹8,000; Akshat's profit share = ₹2,200.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In a partnership (same time period for both), profit share is directly proportional to investment: Akshat's investment / Total investment = Akshat's profit / Total profit.

 

• Akshat's investment = (2,200/8,000) × 57,000.

 

• = 0.275 × 57,000 = ₹15,675.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find Akshat's profit fraction first (2200/8000 = 11/40), then apply this exact fraction to the total investment: (11/40) × 57,000 = 15,675.

 

NOTE

 

• This proportional-share method assumes both partners invested for the same duration; otherwise capital × time (not capital alone) must be used.

question: The sides of a triangle are 85 cm, 13 cm, and 84 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with a length of 13 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 84 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sides of the triangle: 85 cm, 13 cm, 84 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check for a right triangle: 13² + 84² = 169 + 7056 = 7225 = 85². Since this holds, the triangle is right-angled, with the right angle between the sides 13 cm and 84 cm (the two legs), and 85 cm as the hypotenuse.

 

• Since the right angle lies between the sides of length 13 cm and 84 cm, these two sides are already perpendicular to each other — so the altitude drawn to the 13 cm side is simply the other leg, 84 cm.

 

• (Check using area: Area = ½ × 13 × 84 = 546 cm² = ½ × base(13) × height ⇒ height = (2 × 546)/13 = 84 cm.) ✓

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise the Pythagorean triplet 13-84-85 instantly; in any right triangle, the altitude to one leg (taken as base) is simply the other leg, since the legs are already perpendicular.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check whether the given three sides form a Pythagorean triplet first — it drastically simplifies area and altitude calculations.

question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 53, 63, 79, 40, 34, 88, 34, 25 and 25 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 49.

 

GIVEN

 

• Observations: 53, 63, 79, 40, 34, 88, 34, 25, 25 (9 observations in total).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 53 + 63 + 79 + 40 + 34 + 88 + 34 + 25 + 25 = 441.

 

• Arithmetic mean = Sum ÷ Number of observations = 441 ÷ 9 = 49.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Add the numbers in convenient pairs/groups (e.g. 34+34+25+25 = 118, 53+63 = 116, 79+40 = 119, plus 88) to reduce arithmetic slips, then divide by the count of 9 (note the repeated 25 counts as two separate observations).

 

NOTE

 

• Carefully count the total number of observations — here 25 appears twice, giving 9 observations in total, not 8.

question: Mr. Akai starts from Point A and drives 2 km towards south. He then takes a right turn, drives 12 km, turns right and drives 21 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 23 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 19 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 11 km to the west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Path: A → 2 km south → right turn → 12 km → right turn → 21 km → right turn → 23 km → right turn → 19 km → stops at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A as origin (0,0). Facing south, drive 2 km: reach (0,−2).

 

• Right turn from south = facing west; drive 12 km: reach (−12,−2).

 

• Right turn from west = facing north; drive 21 km: reach (−12, 19).

 

• Right turn from north = facing east; drive 23 km: reach (11, 19).

 

• Right turn from east = facing south; drive 19 km: reach (11, 0). This is point P.

 

• P(11,0) to A(0,0): the difference is purely in the x-direction, 11 km, with P to the east of A, so from P, A lies 11 km to the west.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track net displacement along only two axes (north-south, east-west) instead of drawing the full path; opposite-direction movements cancel directly (e.g. south 2 then later south 19 add up, north 21 partly cancels them).

 

NOTE

 

• After each 90° right turn, the facing direction cycles: South → West → North → East → South, and so on.

question: Sarita starts from Point A and drives 8 km towards the west. She then takes a left turn, drives 5 km, turns left and drives 5 km. She then takes a right turn and drives 6 km. She takes a final left turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should she drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 11 km towards the north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Path: A → 8 km west → left turn → 5 km → left turn → 5 km → right turn → 6 km → left turn → 3 km → stops at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A as origin (0,0). Facing west, drive 8 km: reach (−8, 0).

 

• Left turn from west = facing south; drive 5 km: reach (−8, −5).

 

• Left turn from south = facing east; drive 5 km: reach (−3, −5).

 

• Right turn from east = facing south; drive 6 km: reach (−3, −11).

 

• Left turn from south = facing east; drive 3 km: reach (0, −11). This is point P.

 

• P(0,−11) to A(0,0): only the y-coordinate differs, by 11 km, with A lying above (north of) P, so from P, A lies 11 km to the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After each 90° left turn, the facing direction cycles: West → South → East → North → West, and so on — track this quickly instead of redrawing the whole diagram.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever the final x-coordinate matches the starting x-coordinate (as here, both 0), the direct return path is purely north-south (or vice versa).

question:
If 'E' stands for '+', 'F' stands for '−', 'G' stands for '×' and 'H' stands for '÷', what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

72 H 8 G 2 E 10 F 5 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 23.

 

GIVEN

 

• E = '+', F = '−', G = '×', H = '÷'. Expression: 72 H 8 G 2 E 10 F 5 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 72 ÷ 8 × 2 + 10 − 5 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS (division and multiplication first, left to right): 72 ÷ 8 = 9; 9 × 2 = 18.

 

• Then addition/subtraction left to right: 18 + 10 − 5 = 28 − 5 = 23.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Substitute the letter-to-symbol code first, rewrite the whole expression in standard mathematical form, and only then apply BODMAS — this avoids confusion mid-calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Division and multiplication have equal priority and are done left to right; the same applies to addition and subtraction.

question: YPMW is related to CLPT in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GHSQ is related to KDVN. To which of the given options is OZYK related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. SVBH.

 

GIVEN

 

• YPMW → CLPT, and GHSQ → KDVN, following a consistent letter-shift logic based on alphabetical position.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert to positions: Y(25) P(16) M(13) W(23) → C(3) L(12) P(16) T(20). Differences: 3−25=−22≡+4(mod26), 12−16=−4, 16−13=+3, 20−23=−3. Pattern: +4, −4, +3, −3.

 

• Verify with G(7)H(8)S(19)Q(17) → K(11)D(4)V(22)N(14): 11−7=+4, 4−8=−4, 22−19=+3, 14−17=−3. Same pattern confirmed: +4, −4, +3, −3.

 

• Apply to OZYK: O(15)→15+4=19=S; Z(26)→26−4=22=V; Y(25)→25+3=28−26=2=B; K(11)→11−3=8=H.

 

• Result: S, V, B, H = SVBH.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once the fixed position-wise shift pattern (+4, −4, +3, −3) is confirmed from the first pair, simply apply the same four shifts, in the same order, to the four letters of the new word.

 

NOTE

 

• When a letter's shift crosses beyond Z or before A, adjust using modulo 26 (e.g. 28 → 28−26 = 2 = B).

question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. Only two people sit between F and B when counted from the right of F. Only two people sit between B and A when counted from the right of B. Only three people sit between F and E when counted from the right of F. D sits to the immediate left of C. How many people sit between F and G when counted from the left of F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A-G) sit around a circular table facing the centre, with the clue relationships described above (right = clockwise, left = anticlockwise, for a person facing the centre).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix F at position 0 (clockwise numbering 0-6). 'Two people between F and B, counted from the right of F' ⇒ B is 3 steps clockwise from F, so B = 3.

 

• 'Three people between F and E, counted from the right of F' ⇒ E is 4 steps clockwise from F, so E = 4.

 

• 'Two people between B and A, counted from the right of B' ⇒ A is 3 steps clockwise from B = 3+3 = 6, so A = 6.

 

• Positions used: F=0, B=3, E=4, A=6. Remaining positions {1, 2, 5} are for C, D, G.

 

• 'D sits to the immediate left of C' means D is one step anticlockwise from C, i.e. C = D + 1 (clockwise). Among {1,2,5}, only 1 and 2 are adjacent, so D=1, C=2 (C is clockwise-next to D), leaving G = 5.

 

• Final clockwise order: F(0), D(1), C(2), B(3), E(4), G(5), A(6).

 

• 'People between F and G counted from the left of F' means moving anticlockwise from F: F(0)→A(6)→G(5). Only A lies between F and G on this path, so exactly 1 person sits between them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For circular seating facing the centre, treat 'right' as clockwise and 'left' as anticlockwise consistently, and convert every 'X people between P and Q counted from the right/left of P' clue into 'Q is (X+1) steps clockwise/anticlockwise from P' — this turns the whole puzzle into simple modular arithmetic.

 

NOTE

 

• Always fix one person's position first as a reference point (here F = 0) before placing the rest, to avoid confusion with relative directions.

question:
Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

Statements:

All cats are mammals.

No mammals are pets.

Conclusions:

(I) Some pets are cats.

(II) No cat is pet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Only conclusion (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All cats are mammals (A-type). No mammals are pets (E-type).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since 'All cats are mammals' places the entire set of cats inside the set of mammals, and 'No mammals are pets' means the mammals set and pets set are completely separate (disjoint), it follows that cats — being entirely within mammals — must also be completely separate from pets.

 

• This gives the valid derived conclusion: 'No cat is pet', which is exactly Conclusion (II) — so it follows.

 

• Conclusion (I) 'Some pets are cats' directly contradicts the valid conclusion 'No cat is pet' (an I-type statement cannot follow when the corresponding E-type statement is proven true), so it does not follow.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'All A are B' + 'No B are C' always combines (by the standard AEE-1 syllogism pattern) to give 'No A are C' as a valid conclusion.

 

NOTE

 

• In syllogisms, an 'I' type conclusion ('Some ... are ...') and an 'E' type conclusion ('No ... is ...') covering the same two terms can never both be true — always check which one the statements actually support.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 3 1 4 6 9 3 5 7 7 9 3 8 6 3 4 4 2 4 7 3 3 8 7 2 2 7 1 (Right)

How many such even numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 3 1 4 6 9 3 5 7 7 9 3 8 6 3 4 4 2 4 7 3 3 8 7 2 2 7 1.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan every even number in the series and check its immediate neighbours on both sides.

 

• Checking each even number (4, 6, 8, 6, 4, 4, 2, 4, 8, 2, 2) against its neighbours, only the 8 in '...3 3 8 7...' (preceded by 3, an odd number, and followed by 7, also odd) satisfies both conditions.

 

• All other even numbers fail either the 'preceded by odd' or 'followed by odd' condition (most are flanked by another even number on at least one side).

 

• Total count of qualifying even numbers = One.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every even number first, then check only its immediate left and right neighbour — reject it the moment either neighbour turns out even, which quickly narrows down the candidates.

 

NOTE

 

• Always count from left to right as instructed, and treat the very first and last terms as having only one neighbour each (so they can never qualify for a 'preceded and followed' condition).

question: In a certain code language, 'STAR' is coded as '3451' and 'RATE' is coded as '4375'. What is the code for 'E' in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• STAR → 3451; RATE → 4375.

 

SOLUTION

 

• STAR and RATE share three common letters — S, T, A, R and R, A, T, E overlap in A, T, R — while S is unique to STAR and E is unique to RATE.

 

• The digits of STAR's code are {3,4,5,1} and of RATE's code are {4,3,7,5}. The digits common to both codes are {3,4,5} — these must belong to the letters common to both words (A, T, R).

 

• The digit unique to STAR's code (not appearing in RATE's code) is 1 — this must be the code for S, the letter unique to STAR.

 

• Similarly, the digit unique to RATE's code (not appearing in STAR's code) is 7 — this must be the code for E, the letter unique to RATE.

 

• Therefore, the code for 'E' = 7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two coded words share some letters, first identify the letter(s) unique to each word — the digit(s) that appear in only one of the two codes must belong to that word's unique letter(s), letting you crack the answer without decoding every letter.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not assume position-by-position mapping (1st letter → 1st digit) is the actual cipher; here the digits for shared letters (A, T, R) are not fixed across the two words, so only the unique-letter/unique-digit trick reliably works.

question: In a certain code language, 'bring hot food' is coded as 'cf tk rg' and 'food is good' is coded as 'ml do cf'. How is 'food' coded in that language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. cf.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'bring hot food' → 'cf tk rg'; 'food is good' → 'ml do cf'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word common to both given phrases is 'food' (present in both 'bring hot food' and 'food is good').

 

• The code-word common to both coded outputs is 'cf' (present in both 'cf tk rg' and 'ml do cf').

 

• Since only one word is common to the phrases and only one code-word is common to their codes, they must correspond to each other: 'food' = 'cf'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In coded-phrase questions, always look for the word repeated across two given phrases and match it to the code-word repeated across their two given codes.

 

NOTE

 

• This method works cleanly only when exactly one word/code-word is common between the two given phrase-code pairs.

question:
What will come in place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '÷' are interchanged and '−' and '×' are interchanged?

168 + 42 × 14 − 9 ÷ 207 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 85.

 

GIVEN

 

• Original: 168 + 42 × 14 − 9 ÷ 207. Swap rule: '+' ↔ '÷', '−' ↔ '×'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After swapping, '+' becomes '÷', '×' becomes '−', '−' becomes '×', '÷' becomes '+'.

 

• New expression: 168 ÷ 42 − 14 × 9 + 207.
